notes:
Summary: Mid-market product analytics vendor evaluating Redwood Hosted API as a low-friction entry and moving to Dedicated for predictable throughput and data isolation. Primary drivers: reduce per-token cost for high-volume embeddings queries, hit 99th pct latency targets for chat, and meet enterprise security (SAML + KMS)

Recent timeline (bullets):
- 2025-11-20: Intro call (Evan) — interest in quick hosted PoC to validate latency with their parallel search pipeline. Mentioned: 'need predictable tails under 150ms for chat.'
- 2026-01-10: Hosted API demo + SDK walkthrough (SE: Priya) — demoed streaming, tool-calling, embeddings batch upload. Follow-up: send test prompts and golden queries.
- 2026-01-25: PoC kickoff (hosted) — 2-week trial ingesting 150k documents, saw 2x cost vs budget baseline on default settings. Suggested Optimize recommendations applied (kv cache + smaller context windows).
- 2026-02-18: Deep dive call (ff_2026-02-18_4921) — Glydero engineering raised concerns about long-tail latency under peak hour; requested Dedicated capacity options and burst behavior. Requested commitment/ramp schedule example.
- 2026-03-02: Pricing workshop (ff_2026-03-02_5033) — discussed commit bands, monthly reserved GPU hours, burst pool pricing, and overage rates. Glydero prefers fixed-price commit with small month-to-month ramp vs 12-month front load.
- 2026-03-10: Security checklist review — sent KMS integration spreadsheet; Glydero asked for sample SOW language about data residency and audit logs.

Use-case & requirements (shorthand):
- primary: embeddings search (high qps), secondary: chat assistant for product analytics (low-latency 90-150ms target), reranking layer for query refinement.
- throughput target: sustained 600 qps embeddings, spikes to 2.5k qps during campaigns.
- latency SLO: median <40ms for embeddings; 99th pct <200ms for chat (aim 150ms).
- cost sensitivity: mid — willing to commit for 12mo if ramp-friendly and clear burst economics.
- model pref: open models (quantized variants) + fallback to slightly larger variant for quality-sensitive ops.

Open negotiation items:
- Commit levels: Glydero asks for tiered commits with quarterly ramp (start 25% of target first 3mo, 50% next, 100% by month 7).
- Burst pool: need clear per-minute burst entitlement and overage unit price; prefer pooled burst across org not per-route.
- Overage calc: request per-token overage cap and soft-threshold alerts.
- Ramp credits: request ramp credit in first 90 days to absorb PoC spikes.

Who: AE Evan Brooks, SE Priya Patel (technical lead), Legal contact at Glydero: J. Park (procurement), Security reviewer: R. Lin

Next steps (short):
- Evan to send proposed tiered commit schedule and example SOW by 2026-03-15.
- Priya to provide benchmarking artifact for embeddings throughput on recommended quantized model variants.
- Legal to start draft of data residency clause; CSM (Marta) to be looped after contract signed.

Notes/quotes: 'If we can get predictable unit economics with a ramp, Dedicated makes sense — but burst costs must not blow the model.' — Glydero VP Eng
